lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. The science lab is 34 °C, because the aircon is broken.
**Kavya:** We're meant to 'observe a chemical reaction'. I've been staring at this test tube for five minutes. Nothing.
**Kavya:** It's like watching my weekend.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about the bottom of her test tube.
**Narrator:** Shrink down to the size of atoms, and there's a cooking competition going on.
**Arrow:** Hello. I'm Arrow. Head judge.
**Arrow:** Simple rules. You start with ingredients. You finish with a brand-new dish. That's a **chemical reaction**.
**Arrow:** And yes, I'm an arrow. I mean '**turns into**'. I am **not** an equals sign.
**Arrow:** People still call me 'Equals'. I'm in therapy for it. My therapist is a question mark.
**Narrator:** Tonight's final: a celebrity guest chef, a strict auditor, and a contestant who is slowly turning orange.
**Ferris:** Hi. Ferris. I'm an iron nail. Don't mind me.
**Narrator:** Test Tube Kitchen. Episode seven: Nothing Is Lost.
**Narrator:** Round one: the signature dish. Every dish must be a **new substance**.
**Olly:** Hello, Kitchen! Olly! **Oxygen**! Guest chef! I react with EVERYTHING!
**Arrow:** Olly is oxygen. Nobody invites him. He just... joins in.
**Olly:** First up: melted chocolate! Ta-da!
**Arrow:** That's chocolate. It was chocolate before. It's still chocolate. Just... sadder.
**Arrow:** Melting is a **physical change**: **no new substance** is made. And it's **easy to reverse**. Put it in the fridge.
**Olly:** Sugar, dissolved in tea!
**Arrow:** Still sugar. Still tea. Physical.
**Olly:** A fried egg!
**Arrow:** Now that's new. The runny egg has turned into **new substances**, with new properties. You can't un-fry it. A **chemical change**.
**Kavya:** How do I tell if MY test tube reacted? We're not allowed to taste anything. I asked.
**Narrator:** Luckily, reactions usually leave **evidence**. Five signs.
**Olly:** Okay! First sign: a **colour change**!
**Olly:** Sign two! A **gas given off**! Fizzing! Bubbles!
**Olly:** Sign three! A **temperature change**! Hotter, or colder!
**Olly:** Sign four! A **precipitate**! Two solutions mix, and a cloudy **insoluble solid** appears!
**Olly:** And sign five! **Light or sound**! Bangs! Pops! My favourite!
**Arrow:** Remember them as **Cool Guys Take Pretty Lasses**. Colour, Gas, Temperature, Precipitate, Light. I didn't write it.
**Kavya:** My water's bubbling! It's reacting!
**Arrow:** It's boiling. Those bubbles are just **water vapour**. Still water. **Physical**.
**Arrow:** One sign is only a **clue**. The real question: has a **new substance** been made?
**Narrator:** Round two: write the menu. In chemistry, the menu is called an **equation**.
**Arrow:** The ingredients you start with are the **reactants**. The new dishes you make are the **products**.
**Arrow:** And in between: me. The arrow. It means '**turns into**'.
**Olly:** Today's special! Magnesium, cooked with ME!
**Kavya:** WHOA. Okay. That is definitely a reaction.
**Arrow:** **Word equation**: **magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide**. A white powder.
**Olly:** Great equation, Equals!
**Arrow:** My name is Arrow.
**Narrator:** Chemists also write a **symbol equation**, with **formulae**, to **count the atoms**.
**Arrow:** **O₂** means two oxygen atoms, joined. The small **subscript** number counts only the atom before it.
**Olly:** That's me! Two atoms! One gorgeous molecule!
**Arrow:** A **big number** in front, the **coefficient**, multiplies the **whole formula**. **2H₂O** means two water molecules.
**Olly:** So that's... two hydrogen atoms!
**Arrow:** Four. Two molecules, two hydrogens each. **Four hydrogen** and **two oxygen** atoms.
**Arrow:** Olly is very confident, and very often wrong. It's a powerful combination.
**Narrator:** Round three. Every dish must now pass... the **audit**.
**Madam Mass:** Madam Mass. Auditor. I weigh everything going in, and everything coming out.
**Madam Mass:** Atoms are only **rearranged**: none made, none destroyed. So the mass of the **products** equals the mass of the **reactants**.
**Narrator:** The **law of conservation of mass**.
**Madam Mass:** Atoms can't hide, and atoms can't die.
**Kavya:** Um. My magnesium got HEAVIER when I burned it. Did I make atoms?
**Madam Mass:** No.
**Olly:** That was ME! I came in from the air, and joined on!
**Narrator:** Now the opposite. Marble chips fizz in acid in an open flask, and the reading goes **down**.
**Madam Mass:** Carbon dioxide gas **escaped** into the room. Nobody leaves my kitchen without signing out.
**Madam Mass:** In a **sealed** flask, nothing gets in or out, and the total mass stays **exactly the same**.
**Madam Mass:** Twenty-three years. Same mass in, same mass out. I have never been surprised. I would quite like to be.
**Narrator:** So a symbol equation must be **balanced**: the same number of each type of atom on both sides.
**Olly:** Next! Hydrogen, cooked with me! **H₂ + O₂ → H₂O**!
**Madam Mass:** Oxygen atoms: two on the left. One on the right. Unbalanced.
**Olly:** Easy! Just make the water **H₂O₂**!
**Arrow:** That's **hydrogen peroxide**. You've made bleach. **Never change a subscript**. Only put big numbers in front.
**Arrow:** A **2** in front of the water fixes the oxygen. Then a **2** in front of the hydrogen: **2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O**.
**Madam Mass:** Four hydrogen, two oxygen, each side. **Balanced**. Approved.
**Narrator:** Round four: heat. Reactions also **give out**, or **take in**, energy.
**Arrow:** An **exothermic** reaction **gives out** heat, so the surroundings get **hotter**: burning, neutralisation, hand warmers.
**Ferris:** Some hand warmers are just iron rusting, really fast. My life, on fast-forward.
**Arrow:** **Exo** sounds like **exit**: energy exits, so it gets warmer.
**Arrow:** An **endothermic** reaction **takes in** heat, so the surroundings get **colder**. **Endo** sounds like **enter**.
**Kavya:** So my cold pack is pushing cold INTO my hand?
**Arrow:** No. **Heat** flows **out of your hand**, into the reaction. That's why it feels cold.
**Narrator:** The main event: **combustion**. A **fuel** burns in oxygen, releasing energy.
**Olly:** Methane, from the gas cooker! Plenty of me: **complete combustion**! **Methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water**!
**Arrow:** A clean **blue flame**. The **most energy**.
**Narrator:** With **limited** oxygen: **incomplete combustion**. A smoky **yellow flame**, **less energy**, black **soot**, and a guest nobody invited.
**Monty:** Heh. Monty. **Carbon monoxide**. You can't see me. You can't smell me.
**Arrow:** Monty is **toxic**. He stops your blood carrying oxygen.
**Monty:** Nobody can catch me. Except... that **carbon monoxide alarm**. I hate that alarm.
**Kavya:** Oh! So that's why my Bunsen flame is yellow with the air hole closed...
**Narrator:** ...and **blue** with it open. More oxygen mixes in.
**Narrator:** Round five: reaction families. Spot the family, and you can **predict the products**.
**Narrator:** First: Ferris. Still turning orange.
**Ferris:** It's called **rusting**: an **oxidation**. Oxidation means **gaining oxygen**.
**Olly:** You're welcome!
**Ferris:** But oxygen alone can't do it. Rusting needs **oxygen AND water**: **iron + oxygen + water → hydrated iron oxide**.
**Arrow:** In completely **dry air**, or in **boiled water** with the air driven out, Ferris won't rust.
**Ferris:** That's why we paint bridges: to keep out oxygen and water. I'd love a coat of paint.
**Narrator:** The opposite is **reduction**: **losing oxygen**. Heat iron oxide with carbon, and the carbon takes the oxygen away.
**Olly:** **Thermal decomposition**! Heat breaks **one compound** into **simpler** ones: green **copper carbonate** into black **copper oxide**, and **carbon dioxide**!
**Narrator:** Bubble that gas through **limewater**: it turns **milky**. The test for **carbon dioxide**.
**Narrator:** **Neutralisation**: **acid + base → salt + water**.
**Arrow:** **A, B, S, W**. Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide make **sodium chloride**, and water. Salt. On a cooking show. Finally.
**Narrator:** And **displacement**: a **more reactive** metal pushes a less reactive one out of its compound.
**Ferris:** Put me in blue **copper sulfate**, and I push the copper out. I'm **more reactive** than copper!
**Ferris:** I'm coated in copper! I'm shiny! I'm WINNING!
**Arrow:** First time I've ever seen Ferris happy. It's unsettling.
**Narrator:** The final round: speed. An explosion is over in a flash. Rusting takes years.
**Arrow:** The **rate** is how fast reactants turn into products. To react, particles must **collide**, with enough energy.
**Narrator:** Raise the **temperature**: particles move faster, so they collide **more often**, and **harder**.
**Narrator:** Raise the **concentration**: more particles crammed into the same space, so **more collisions**.
**Olly:** Like the MRT at rush hour!
**Narrator:** Increase the **surface area**: crush a lump into **powder**, and far more of it can be hit.
**Narrator:** And finally... a **catalyst**.
**Arrow:** This is Kat. She's a **catalyst**. She **speeds up** a reaction, **without being used up**.
**Arrow:** She gives particles an **easier route** to react, then walks off, completely unchanged.
**Olly:** Ooh! So she makes MORE food!
**Arrow:** No. Same products. Same amount. Just **faster**.
**Narrator:** Living things use catalysts called **enzymes**. **Amylase**, in saliva, speeds up the breakdown of starch.
**Kavya:** That's why bread tastes sweeter if you chew it for ages. I've been chewing this for three minutes.
**Narrator:** And a car's **catalytic converter**, with metals like **platinum**, turns carbon monoxide into **carbon dioxide**.
**Monty:** Carbon dioxide? Me? I'm going to be so... boring.

chapters.title: The judges save you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the judges decide, the cast would like to save you some marks.
**Arrow:** One. Equations use an **arrow**. Never an equals sign. Please.
**Olly:** Two! Balance with **big numbers** in front. Never change a subscript! I learned the hard way!
**Madam Mass:** Three. Mass is **never destroyed**. If it seems to drop, a **gas escaped**.
**Ferris:** Four. Rusting needs **oxygen and water**. Not just air.
**Monty:** Five. Incomplete combustion makes **carbon monoxide** and soot. Not just carbon dioxide. Write ME.
**Arrow:** Six. Temperature **rises**: **exothermic**. Temperature **falls**: **endothermic**.
**Narrator:** And the winner of Test Tube Kitchen is...
**Arrow:** Ferris. Copper, pushed out of copper sulfate. Genuinely new substances. Well done.
**Ferris:** I won? I'm so happy, I could rust.
**Narrator:** Test Tube Kitchen will return.
**Arrow:** Kat. Twelve reactions today. You must be exhausted.
**Madam Mass:** Five point zero zero grams. Same as this morning.
**Kat:** ...Again.
